classification_signals: The abstract states the essay 'analyzes the design and aleatory determinants that prime atmospheric effects' and proposes 'orchestrat[ing] different architectural generators'.

The paper explicitly introduces and elaborates on an 'atmospheric equation' and categorizes 'four categories of determinants' (physiological, personal, sociocultural, spatial) and 'experimental determinants' (pages 8-9).
It further systematizes 'generators of architectural atmosphere' into gestural, sensorial, and contextual types (pages 13-14).

The 'Lesson' section (page 15) discusses the impossibility of a simple 'recipe' for atmosphere and outlines two strategies for designers, indicating a theoretical conclusion rather than empirical results.

The paper extensively cites and synthesizes existing literature from philosophy, architecture, and neuroscience to build its framework, without presenting new empirical data or a specific methodology section for data collection/analysis.
The 'Acknowledgements' mention the paper is a 'legacy' of a symposium and part of a research project, suggesting a synthesis of ideas.
title: Generators of Architectural Atmosphere

findings.quote: Atmosphere is the whole of affective meanings identifying a situation or place that allows us to resonate and tune into our surroundings.
The complexity of atmosphere is well known [F1].

findings.consequent: Bodies emotionally resonate with the multisensory entirety of forms, materials, shades, colors, sounds, and scents
findings.quote: Staging atmospheres is a compositional task in which we orchestrate different architectural generators to let our bodies emotionally resonate with the multisensory entirety of forms, materials, shades, colors, sounds, and scents that constitute a place.
Designed atmospheres become generators of identity and meaning.

findings.antecedent: Ways we organize space and buildings
findings.consequent: Protection from elements and meaningful experience
findings.quote: “Architecture is,” in fact, "ideally located at the intersection of [two] complementary aspects of our lives (i.e., fitness and flourishing),” confirms the philosopher Mark Johnson, “insofar as the ways we organize space and buildings address simultaneously our need for protection from the elements and our need for meaningful experience” (2018, 242).

findings.consequent: Meaning and significance from ways it organises our bodily perception and experience
findings.quote: An intriguing premise is “architecture gets much of its meaning and significance from the ways it organises our bodily perception and experience" (Johnson 2002, 84).
Atmosphere is the emotional-affective component of lived space that allows us to resonate and tune into our surroundings.
From an embodied perspective, we may assume if the bodily resonance is significantly aroused, it influences the subject's affective attunement accordingly (Fuchs and Koch 2014).

“The judgement of environmental character is,” indeed, as Juhani Pallasmaa emphasizes, “a complex multisensory fusion of countless factors which are immediately and synthetically grasped as an overall atmosphere” (2014, 230).
The premise behind this complexity is “atmosphere is the prototypical 'between'-phenomenon. [...] [It] is something between the subject and the object" (Böhme 1998, 112).

findings.antecedent: Physiological determinants (structural properties of human body)
findings.consequent: Body resonance process activated by atmospheric affordances, triggering and conditioning nonconscious emotions
findings.quote: The physiological determinants are those related to the structural properties of the human body. They exert a significant sway on the body resonance process activated by atmospheric affordances, triggering and conditioning nonconscious emotions (both interoceptive and proprioceptive feedback).
Since emotions are somatic correlates of conscious feelings and mutually interact, physiological determinants affect conscious feelings as well.

findings.consequent: More accurate perception and understanding of surroundings
findings.quote: The hypothesis is that people who are more interoceptively sensitive (that is, more attuned to their internal body signals and clues) are more accurate in how they perceive and understand their surroundings (Murphy Paul 2021).
Sociocultural patterns prime our emotional reactions to atmospheres by acting upon our bodies.

Spatial determinants afford emotionally significant invitations. Such affective affordances are so closely interconnected to each other they cannot always be traced back to a specific material source.
Architects have the task (or, simply the desire) to design and stage atmospheres, given architecture “produces atmospheres in everything it creates” (Böhme 1991, 36).

findings.antecedent: Geometric structures and corporeal constellations (architectural generators)
findings.consequent: Conditions under which an atmosphere can appear
findings.quote: Philosopher Gernot Böhme articulates, “the making of atmospheres is restricted to the arrangement of the conditions under which an atmosphere can appear" (2013b, 161) [F6]. He calls these designable, determinant conditions generators.⁴⁸ They “are above all the geometric structures and corporeal constellations” (Böhme 2013c, 93) the architect installs⁴⁹ and can be "of an objective kind" (including material details affording motor interactions) or as “non-objective or non-physical," as light and sound (Böhme, 92).

findings.antecedent: Gestural generators of atmosphere (dimension, proportions, forms, geometry)
findings.consequent: Movement and kinesthetic impressions (e.g., sensations of volume, load, density)
findings.quote: Gestural generators of atmosphere (such as dimension, proportions, forms, and geometry), distinguished by their ability to suggest movement and kinesthetic impressions (e.g., sensations of volume, load, and density, which can render a space oppressive, solemn, vast, or poignant).

findings.antecedent: Sensorial generators of atmosphere (light conditions, colors, materials, textures)
findings.consequent: Specific sensory stimuli (visual, sounds, scents, tactile feedback)
findings.quote: Sensorial generators of atmosphere (such as light conditions, colors, materials, and textures), which produce specific sensory stimuli (among which are visual inputs, sounds, scents, and tactile feedback) that transpire from the architectonic materiality through their sensuous effects and are initially perceived in aggregate.
Sight, hearing, scent, and touch are the key sensory channels for perceiving architectural atmospheres.

findings.antecedent: Ways space is used by its inhabitants
findings.source: Page 17, citing Martin, Nettleton, and Buse 2020
findings.quote: Ultimately, we should recognize that “the atmospheric qualities of place are related to the ways in which space is used by its inhabitants, rather than the intentions of its architects per se" (Martin, Nettleton, and Buse 2020, 85).

limitations: Systematic research and empirical evidence on the emotional impact of architectural atmospheres (or, in a broader sense, the built environment) are still few, and methodologies differ.

The atmospheric qualities of place are related to the ways in which space is used by its inhabitants, rather than the intentions of its architects per se, making the atmospheric equation more complicated.
Deciphering the mechanisms that generate architectural atmospheres is analogous to synthesizing the essence of architecture composition, which is impossible; there is no 'recipe' for right and wrong.
minimum_safe_summary: This theoretical paper by Elisabetta Canepa proposes an "atmospheric equation" to understand how architectural atmospheres are generated and influence human experience. It categorizes determinants into physiological, personal, sociocultural, spatial, and experimental factors, and further details spatial "generators" (gestural, sensorial, contextual) that contribute to atmosphere through multisensory stimuli. Key findings include the idea that atmosphere is a complex, multisensory fusion that elicits bodily resonance and affective attunement, and that architecture's meaning derives from how it organizes bodily perception. The paper concludes that empirical evidence on the emotional impact of built environments is still scarce, and that atmospheric qualities are ultimately shaped by inhabitants' use of space rather than solely architects' intentions, making the "atmospheric equation" inherently complex and difficult to fully quantify.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Human experience of space is embodied, multi-sensory, and pre-reflective, forming the fundamental basis for architectural atmosphere.

Architectural atmosphere is an emergent, holistic quality generated through the synthesis of material qualities, light, sound, hapticity, scale, time, and cultural associations, experienced affectively.

mechanism_chain.description: The paper describes how various architectural elements and sensory qualities combine to generate a holistic, affective architectural atmosphere through embodied perception.

steps.from_construct: Architectural elements (e.g., light, shadow, material texture, sound, scale, proportion, time, memory)
